slides.title: Writing Well Is Not the Same as Generating Insight
bullets: A well-captured insight can still fail if written up poorly
Vague, buried or missing detail kills its usefulness
Writing an actionable insight deserves deliberate practice

slides.title: A Written Insight Should Answer Five Things
bullets: What was observed and why it matters
Who it affects and what action is realistically feasible now
How anyone would know whether that action worked
Not every insight needs all five spelled out in full formal detail

slides.title: Put the Insight First, Not the Visit Story
bullets: Colleagues scanning dozens of reports need the substance up front
State the insight itself in the first sentence
Supporting detail and quotes follow, they don't precede it

slides.title: State the Evidentiary Basis Explicitly
bullets: Say how many physicians, over what timeframe, how consistently
Don't imply a broad pattern from a single conversation
Distinguish clearly between one physician and multiple independent physicians

slides.title: Name a Next Step or Owner
bullets: A concrete suggestion makes an insight far more likely to be used
Example: flag it to the evidence-generation team for the RWE protocol
The MSL isn't expected to solve it, just to point the way

slides.title: Avoid Jargon Only Your Team Understands
bullets: Insights travel across functions with no first-hand context of the visit
They reach Medical Advisors, evidence teams and filtered Market Access channels
The writing itself must carry the full meaning

takeaway.title: An insight only works if it's written to be understood and acted on by others
bullets: Lead with the insight itself, not the visit narrative
State the evidentiary basis honestly, not an implied broad pattern
Name a plausible next step so the insight actually gets used
